# Functions of the standard library that are `pure` and return data (a string, bytes, a slice, a map,
# a struct, a pointer, an interface), each read and found not to carry the text of an argument.
# See bench/README.md, "When a function may be pure", and TestPureFunctionsThatReturnDataAreReviewed.
# A function whose result can hold an argument is not here: it has a `flows:` (R-03).

(*database/sql.Conn).BeginTx  # a handle of a database: what it returns is the stored data (the sources of the rules), not the arguments
(*database/sql.DB).Begin  # a handle of a database: what it returns is the stored data (the sources of the rules), not the arguments
(*database/sql.DB).BeginTx  # a handle of a database: what it returns is the stored data (the sources of the rules), not the arguments

(*log/slog.Logger).Handler  # a logger or an attribute: goes to a log, not read back
(*mime/multipart.Writer).FormDataContentType  # a boundary (random), or a writer whose writes go to its argument (a known limit: the flow into the writer does not reach the destination)
(*net/http.Transport).Clone  # a handle or a value of the runtime or the network: not the text of an argument
(*net/smtp.Client).Data  # a handle or a value of the runtime or the network: not the text of an argument

(*net/url.URL).Port  # digits only (the parser checks them)
